NDT training in Delaware: how it works for Delaware employers and technicians

NDT training for Delaware employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT live online or onsite at your facility, from Wilmington and New Castle down to Dover and Sussex County, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A for Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training, experience, exams and a vision test.

Delaware is small, but its NDT market is not. The state sits in the middle of the Delaware Valley industrial corridor, where refineries, chemical plants, power stations, a busy river port and major bridges are strung along both banks of the Delaware River from Philadelphia to the bay. Many Delaware-based technicians work across state lines in a single month, in New Castle County one week, in southeastern Pennsylvania or South Jersey the next. That makes a portable, well-documented SNT-TC-1A programme especially valuable here.

Atlantis has no training centre in Delaware. Theory is taught live online and practical training takes place onsite at your shop or plant. This section adds depth to the overview above: course-by-course detail, the certification path, scheduling, the regulatory position on radiography in a non-Agreement State, employer services and a Delaware-specific FAQ.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Delaware

MethodLevelsWhat Delaware employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (Ultrasonic Testing)I, II, IIIThickness surveys on refinery and chemical piping, weld inspection on repairs, vessel and tank shell checksLevel I: none beyond the written practice. Level II: UT Level I plus experience
PAUT (Phased Array UT)II, IIICorrosion mapping, weld inspection on pressure equipment, power plant component inspectionNormally UT Level II
TOFD (Time of Flight Diffraction)II, IIICrack sizing on thick-wall welds for fitness-for-service assessmentsNormally UT Level II
RT (Radiographic Testing)I, II, IIIASME B31.3 process piping welds, pipeline tie-ins, castings and valve bodiesRadiation safety training and NRC radiographer certification for isotope work; RT Level I before Level II
MT (Magnetic Particle Testing)I, II, IIICarbon steel vessel and structural welds, bridge and port crane steel, marine fabricationLevel I: none. Level II: MT Level I plus experience
PT (Liquid Penetrant Testing)I, II, IIIStainless and nickel-alloy equipment in chemical service, aluminium and non-ferrous partsLevel I: none. Level II: PT Level I plus experience
VT (Visual Testing)I, II, IIIInternal equipment inspections, weld checks, bridge and structural condition surveysLevel I: none; usually first
ET (Eddy Current Testing)I, II, IIIHeat exchanger tube inspection, aircraft skin and fastener inspection, surface cracks through coatingsLevel I: none. Level II: ET Level I plus experience

Ultrasonic Testing. The UT course builds from the physics of sound in steel to calibration, thickness measurement and angle-beam weld examination. Delaware refinery and chemical work means a lot of corrosion monitoring on piping circuits, so we cover measurement repeatability, high-temperature readings, coatings and how poor data leads to wrong remaining-life calculations. Level II adds indication evaluation and procedure writing.

Phased Array and TOFD. For UT Level II technicians, PAUT and TOFD courses cover probe and wedge selection, focal laws, scan plans, encoded scanning, sizing and data review. Advanced UT is increasingly specified on the region's refinery and power work where owners want recorded, reviewable data rather than a pass/fail note.

Radiographic Testing. RT covers radiation physics, exposure and geometry, image quality indicators, film and digital techniques and weld interpretation. Because Delaware is not an NRC Agreement State, the radiation safety context is taught with federal NRC requirements in mind, which differs from what a technician trained in a neighbouring Agreement State such as Pennsylvania or New Jersey may have heard.

Magnetic Particle and Penetrant. MT covers yokes, prods, coils, continuous and residual techniques and fluorescent inspection; PT covers penetrant systems, removal methods, dwell and development and the effects of contamination. Chemical plants run a wide mix of alloys, so we spend time on when MT is not an option and why sulfur- and halogen-controlled penetrant materials matter on stainless and nickel alloys.

Visual Testing. VT covers direct and remote visual examination, lighting and access, weld and corrosion measurement and reporting. It is the usual first certification and remains central to bridge, port and plant inspection.

Eddy Current Testing. ET covers impedance-plane analysis, probe selection, frequency choice and calibration standards, with applications in exchanger tubing and in aircraft structure inspection.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Delaware, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer's document sets the rules for every method and level, including training and experience minimums, exams, vision testing and recertification.
  2. Classroom training. Completed and documented to those minimums; the figures by method and level are in our training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged under supervision. For Delaware technicians who work across state lines, keep experience records by job and method so a future employer can verify them.
  4. General exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as ASME Section V and B31.3, API inspection codes or AWS D1.1.
  6. Practical exam on real flawed specimens, administered or overseen by the designated Level III.
  7. Vision test: near-vision and colour-contrast, repeated annually.
  8. Employer certification, signed and filed.
  9. Recertification on the interval your written practice sets.

For the full background, read our SNT-TC-1A certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Delaware crews

  • Live online theory for individuals and small groups anywhere in the state. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite training at your facility in New Castle, Kent or Sussex County, using your instruments and specimens, led under ASNT Level III oversight.
  • Blended programmes that spread theory over several weeks online and finish with a practical and exam block onsite.

Scheduling around outages matters in the Delaware Valley. Refinery and chemical turnarounds, spring and autumn power plant outages on both sides of the river, and marine and bridge work that follows the weather all compete for the same technicians. We schedule onsite blocks into the quieter weeks and can split groups so work continues. Send your headcount and window for a cohort or onsite quote within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Delaware crew, or see our corporate NDT training page.

Where NDT technicians work in Delaware

Refining and chemicals. The Delaware City refinery is a complex East Coast refinery and a major mechanical-integrity and turnaround employer. Specialty-chemical and materials companies headquartered or operating in the Wilmington and New Castle area add steady inspection work across a wide range of alloys. Across the river and up the corridor sit further refineries and chemical plants in New Jersey and Pennsylvania that Delaware inspection companies commonly serve.

Power and nuclear. Gas-fired generating stations operate around Wilmington, and the Salem and Hope Creek nuclear stations sit on Artificial Island on the New Jersey side of the river, directly across from Delaware. Nuclear owners apply ASME Section XI and their own qualification requirements in addition to SNT-TC-1A, so technicians targeting nuclear outage work should check the owner's programme.

Military aviation. Dover Air Force Base operates large strategic airlift aircraft. Military aircraft NDI is performed by trained Air Force personnel under the service's own technical orders, while contractors and suppliers supporting aviation maintenance work to their customers' qualification requirements, commonly NAS 410. We do not offer NAS 410 certification, but our ET, PT and UT method courses build the underlying knowledge.

Port and marine. The Port of Wilmington handles heavy cargo, and cranes, berths, barges and marine structures need MT, UT and VT on welded steel.

Bridges and transportation. The Delaware Memorial Bridge twin spans, managed by the Delaware River and Bay Authority, and DelDOT's state bridge inventory generate steel bridge inspection and fabrication NDT, typically to AWS bridge welding requirements.

Natural gas. Distribution and transmission operators serving the Delmarva Peninsula, including a Dover-headquartered energy company, need weld inspection for pipeline construction and repair under PHMSA rules and API 1104. The Delaware Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety.

Industrial radiography in Delaware. Delaware is not an NRC Agreement State. The NRC, through its Region I office in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, licenses and inspects radioactive-material use in Delaware, including industrial radiography with isotope sources. Under 10 CFR Part 34, radiographers using sealed sources must be certified through an NRC-recognised certification programme, such as the ASNT Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel programme, or an Agreement State programme. X-ray equipment is registered with the state's Office of Radiation Control. Your SNT-TC-1A RT certificate proves NDT competence; it is separate from those radiation safety requirements.

Working the whole corridor. Because Delaware crews regularly cross into Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Maryland, the radiation rules they meet change with the job. Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Maryland are Agreement States with their own radiation control programmes, while work on the Delaware side falls under the NRC for radioactive materials. A Delaware inspection company running isotope crews on both sides of the river therefore has to manage licensing, reciprocity notifications and radiographer certification carefully, and its technicians should understand why the paperwork differs from one site to the next. Our RT course explains the framework in plain language so technicians know what to ask their radiation safety officer, while the licensing itself stays with the employer. The same cross-border reality applies to NDT certification: because SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer rather than the state, a technician certified by a Delaware company carries that certification to every site the company sends them, provided the customer accepts the employer's written practice.

What Delaware employers ask for. SNT-TC-1A Level II in the requested method, code experience (ASME, API 1104, AWS D1.1), site safety training, and TWIC for port work. Plant work often pairs technicians with API-certified inspectors. Some employers serving international clients also mention ISO 9712; Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only and does not offer ISO 9712, API or CWI training. See our NDT salary guide for pay context.

Level III services and written practices for Delaware NDT companies

Many Delaware inspection companies are small firms serving a few large plants. Their written practice is often inherited, out of date, or silent on PAUT and TOFD. When a refinery or utility audits them, gaps show up quickly. Atlantis offers:

  • Written practice development and revision aligned to current SNT-TC-1A and to the methods you perform.
  • Outside Level III services for exam administration, specimen control and certification sign-off.
  • Record audits and recertification tracking.
  • ASNT Level III preparation for senior technicians.

We also see a specific Delaware pattern: technicians certified years ago by a previous employer, now working for a small local firm that has simply accepted the old certificates. Under SNT-TC-1A that is not enough. The new employer must review the technician's training and experience records against its own written practice, examine the technician as that document requires, and issue its own certification. We run that re-qualification process efficiently, typically combining a records review, targeted refresher training and examinations in a single onsite visit, so experienced people are not pulled off the job for longer than necessary.

Practise before the practical exam

Our Practical NDT 3D simulator offers practice in 12 methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Delaware trainees use it to rehearse technique between online sessions. It is a practice tool and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees Atlantis course content, written practices and examinations.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Delaware

How do I get NDT certified in Delaware?

Work for an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete classroom training and logged experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer certifies you.

Can I take NDT training online in Delaware?

Yes, for classroom hours accepted by your employer's written practice. Practical work and exams must be hands-on, which we deliver onsite.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Classroom training is a matter of weeks; experience takes months. The minimums are in our training requirements matrix and your written practice.

Do I need a license for radiography in Delaware?

For isotope radiography the employer needs an NRC licence, and radiographers need NRC-recognised radiographer certification. X-ray equipment must be registered with the state. Your SNT-TC-1A RT certificate is a separate requirement.

What does NDT training cost in Delaware?

It depends on method, level, group size and format. We do not publish prices; quotes come back within one business day. Request a Delaware training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Delaware employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for NDT personnel across Delaware Valley refining, chemical, power and fabrication work.

Do you have a training centre in Wilmington?

No. We train online and onsite at employers' facilities.

Is my certification valid if I work in Pennsylvania or New Jersey?

SNT-TC-1A certification is tied to your employer, not to a state. If your employer sends you across the river, your certification goes with the job.

Which method should I start with?

VT, PT or MT are the usual first steps, followed by UT. They lead quickly to employable work in plants and fabrication shops.

Do you offer ISO 9712 or API training?

No. Atlantis is SNT-TC-1A only. Some Delaware employers also ask for those schemes, but SNT-TC-1A is the foundation used by most US plant owners.

Can you help with our first customer audit?

Yes. Our Level III reviews your written practice and records and closes the gaps.
